Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we committed to:  

Summary of what we heard:
- Pilot scope: 2 inference endpoints (search re-ranker + customer-response assistant) running at 99th P95 latency < 300ms for UI flows.
- Expected steady-state monthly volume: 50M–180M tokens depending on ramp and regen rate.
- Primary procurement path: PO + SOW (legal review expected).

Deliverables I said I would follow up with:
1) A conservative monthly spend band (low / mid / high) tied to token volumes and a target $/1M figure.
2) Procurement thresholds and typical approval lead times for each band.
3) Simple token-econ workbook to validate assumptions.

I'll attach the spreadsheet with a couple of scenarios. If you want, we can do a short working session with your finance/vendor team to lock the band that maps to your PO size.

Next steps from our side:
- Send token econ file (attached) and a short note you can forward to procurement.
- Schedule a 30-min finance walkthrough (Monica will help coordinate availability).

If this capture looks right, let me know who on your side should be copied into the finance/procurement thread (name + email) and any internal PO threshold we should be aware of.

Cheers,
Jonas

Thanks Jonas — this is exactly the level of detail procurement needs. A few clarifying points from our side:  

- Our initial PO authority thresholds: individual POs up to $20k can be approved by Engineering Purchasing. Anything > $20k requires Finance + Legal review.
- For multi-month pilots we typically issue a single PO that covers the pilot term (90 days) and then convert to a contract if we proceed.
- Can you include a target $/1M tokens with and without prefix caching (we expect ~30% cache hit for the re-ranker)?

I've looped procurement on this email — they may propose a terms checklist shortly. Please make the token-econ sheet clear on assumptions (prompt length, completion tokens, cache).

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product — Orchard AI
elena@orchard.ai

Elena / Procurement team — thanks for the thresholds and the cache note. Attached are two items:  
- redwood-token-econ.xlsx (has three scenarios and explicit cache assumptions)
- pilot-scope-and-ops.docx (short SOW template + ops onboarding checklist)

Top-line unit economics (illustrative, conservative assumptions):
- Scenario A (low): 50M tokens/month → baseline unit $/1M tokens = $900 (no cache). With 30% prefix cache applied to re-ranker flows, effective $/1M ~ $750.
- Scenario B (mid): 120M tokens/month → baseline $/1M = $650. With 30% cache, effective $/1M ~ $550.
- Scenario C (high): 180M tokens/month → baseline $/1M = $520. With 30% cache, effective $/1M ~ $420.

Suggested monthly spend bands (to align with PO authority):
- Band 1: $45k–$110k / month (maps to 50M–120M tokens) — typically handled via PO under $120k (single PO under $20k monthly equivalent may still require review).
- Band 2: $110k–$300k / month (maps to 120M–320M tokens) — requires Finance + Legal sign-off, 2–3 week lead time for contract review.
- Band 3: $300k+ / month — enterprise contract and SLAs, multi-week procurement cycle, reserved capacity recommended.

Procurement/approval guidance:
- For Orchard's stated PO threshold ($20k), a 90-day pilot at Band 1 will likely exceed single-PO approval if you try to cover full term in one PO. Two options: 1) Split into monthly POs under $20k (administratively heavy) or 2) Finance issues a single pilot PO and signs off as an exception — we've seen both approaches.
- Typical legal review on our side for PO+SOW pilots is 3–5 business days once SOW is in place. Finance sign-off usually 2–4 business days.

If helpful, we can put together a 1-page procurement memo that spells out the unit econ and recommended PO path for your finance approver.

Action items I propose:
- Monica to schedule a 30-min walk-through with your procurement/finance this week.
- Marissa will prepare the procurement memo + a short pricing appendix tied to the attached workbook.

Let me know preferred time slots and any internal PO/contract constraints we didn't capture.

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
